content: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir is indicated for the treatment of patients with hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotypes 1 through 6, either without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis. It is also approved for treatment-experienced patients with genotype 1 who have previously been treated with a regimen containing either an NS5A inhibitor or an NS3/4A protease inhibitor, but not both. The recommended dosage is three tablets (300 mg/120 mg total dose) taken orally once daily. Prior to initiating HCV treatment with glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, patients should be tested for evidence of current or prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection by measuring hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc). For children aged 3 years and older, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir is indicated for treatment-naïve patients with chronic HCV genotypes 1 through 6, either without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis. It is also indicated for treatment-experienced children aged 3 years and older with HCV genotype 1 who have been previously treated with a regimen containing either an NS5A inhibitor or an NS3/4A protease inhibitor, but not both. The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established in children under 3 years of age. Testing for current or prior HBV infection is recommended before initiating HCV treatment. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir interacts with several medications, either increasing or decreasing their levels or effects. These interactions are primarily mediated through hepatic and intestinal enzymes, such as CYP3A4, or transport proteins, such as P-glycoprotein (P-gp), OATP1B1, and OATP1B3. Below are specific interactions and recommendations: 1. Elagolix: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases elagolix levels. Concomitant use with strong OATP1B1 inhibitors is contraindicated. 2. Rifampin: Rifampin decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by increasing metabolism. Concomitant use is contraindicated. 3. Apalutamide: Apalutamide decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Atazanavir: Atazanavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels, raising the risk of ALT elevations. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Atorvastatin: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases atorvastatin levels, potentially increasing the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Concomitant use is not recommended. 6. Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Colchicine: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases colchicine levels. Avoid use in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the colchicine dose. 8. Cyclosporine: Cyclosporine increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid if the cyclosporine dose exceeds 100 mg/day. 9. Darunavir: Darunavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid coadministration. 10. Efavirenz: Efavirenz decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Enasidenib: Enasidenib increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid coadministration or adjust the substrate dosage if unavoidable. 12. Enzalutamide: Enzalutamide decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Fexinidazole: Fexinidazole increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Ivosidenib: Ivosidenib decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid coadministration or monitor for therapeutic loss. 15. Lasmiditan: Lasmiditan increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Leniolisib: Leniolisib increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Lopinavir: Lopinavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid coadministration. 18. Lovastatin: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases lovastatin levels, raising the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Concomitant use is not recommended. 19. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir: These drugs increase glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Phenytoin: Phenytoin decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Primidone: Primidone decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Repotrectinib: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases repotrectinib levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Resmetirom: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases resmetirom levels. Avoid coadministration. 24. Simvastatin: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases simvastatin levels, raising the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Concomitant use is not recommended. 25. St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid coadministration. 26. Sulbactam/Durlobactam: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases sulbactam levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Tepotinib: Tepotinib increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid or reduce the substrate dosage if necessary. 28. Trofinetide: Trofinetide increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid coadministration. 29. Tucatinib: Tucatinib increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Avoid or reduce the substrate dosage if necessary. 30. Zavegepant (intranasal): Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases zavegepant levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
